title: My room at WKU
paragraphs: My name is Aizhan and I live in the WKU student dormitory. My room is on the fourth floor — Room 412. It is a small but comfortable room. I share it with my roommate Zarina. Our room has everything we need for studying and sleeping. I am very happy with my room!

This is my desk. It is next to the window, so I have good natural light when I study. On this desk, I have my laptop, my notebook, three pens, and a dictionary. That dictionary is very important — it is an English-Kazakh dictionary and I use it every day. My desk is always clean and organised.

These are my textbooks on the shelf above the desk. I have six textbooks this semester: English, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, History of Kazakhstan, and Physical Education. That big red book is my English textbook — it is my favourite! Those small books are my notebooks for each subject.

This is my wardrobe. It is not very big, but it is enough for my clothes. I have two pairs of jeans, four t-shirts, two sweaters, one jacket, and my formal clothes for university presentations. That blue sweater is my favourite — my grandmother made it for me. Those shoes under the wardrobe are my everyday sneakers.

On my bedside table, I have three important things. This is my phone charger — I never forget it! That small plant is a cactus. My mother gave it to me before I left home. She said: "This cactus is strong — just like you!" I love this little cactus. And those headphones are for listening to music and online English classes.

I also have a small mirror on the wall and a poster of Kazakhstan above my bed. That poster has a beautiful photo of the Altai mountains. These mountains are in East Kazakhstan and they are amazing. Zarina has a poster of Paris on her side of the room. We have very different tastes!

My favourite object in this room is my laptop. This laptop is two years old but it still works perfectly. I use it for everything — watching lectures, writing essays, video calls with my family, and studying English grammar. Without this laptop, university life would be very difficult for me.

Every morning, I make my bed and organise my desk before breakfast. My mother taught me this habit. She always says: "A clean room means a clean mind!" I agree with her. When my room is tidy, I can concentrate better and study more effectively. I am proud of my little room — it is my home away from home!

dialogue.speaker: Dias
dialogue.text: Aizhan, show me your room! I want to see how you live.

dialogue.speaker: Aizhan
dialogue.text: Okay, look! This is my room — Room 412. Not big, but cosy!

dialogue.speaker: Dias
dialogue.text: Oh, nice! What is that on your desk?

dialogue.speaker: Aizhan
dialogue.text: This is my laptop. And that big book is my English dictionary.

dialogue.speaker: Dias
dialogue.text: What are those books on the shelf?

dialogue.speaker: Aizhan
dialogue.text: These are my textbooks — one for each subject. That red one is English.

dialogue.speaker: Dias
dialogue.text: And what is that small green thing on the table?

dialogue.speaker: Aizhan
dialogue.text: Ha! That is my cactus. My mum gave it to me. I call it "Strong"!

dialogue.speaker: Dias
dialogue.text: That's so cute! What is that poster on the wall?

dialogue.speaker: Aizhan
dialogue.text: Those are the Altai mountains! Beautiful, right? I love Kazakhstan.

dialogue.speaker: Dias
dialogue.text: Your room looks really comfortable. My room is very messy!

dialogue.speaker: Aizhan
dialogue.text: Ha! Clean room, clean mind — my mother's rule. Try it!
